text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The UN-sponsored committee against torture has recommended that Namibia set up independent agencies to inspect the country's detention centres and prisons as well as allegations of police misconduct.

Peace and development cannot be achieved if violence against women and children continues in Namibia, Director of the Department of Women Affairs Netumbo Ndaitwah said at the first national hearing on violence against women and children, which got underway in Windhoek yesterday.

Namibian land baron Werner List announced at President Sam Nujoma's birthday party yesterday that he is doanting six farms belonging to the Ohlthaver & List group to the government to be used to resettle landless people and establish an agricultural college.
